I've recently found a need to upgrade some of the production systems I'm responsible for managing, since the release we've standardized on does not support newer versions of software that we need to mitigate attacks we've received.

After looking into various distros, I've realised that nearly all of them have been infected by the systemd cancer, and are therefore undesirable. My reasons for avoiding systemd are many, but include the binary log issue, the monolithic structure of the codebase (even if it's modular, you can't use logind without systemd, which breaks most systems), the possibility of M$ and NSA interference, and the reputation that Poettering brings to the table after the unstable debacle that was PulseAudio. Considering this system will be supporting five-figure user numbers, it needs to be stable, and the fact that a corrupt journal log can crash a server is completely unacceptable.

I'd like to avoid the BSDs for now, as our support and admin staff aren't trained in their use, only CentOS and Windows, and I'd prefer to make the transfer as seamless as possible, for both admins and support staff.

I've found information that Gentoo and Slackware are providing an alternative to systemd, but the fact that Gentoo needs to be compiled at installation doesn't strike me as production-ready or easily supportable, and I read a rumor that Slackware only compiled 800 of the 1400 or so packages for its latest version, with older packages reused from previous releases, which makes me doubt their ability to provide ongoing support in the case of a catastrophic failure.

Can anyone provide suggestions or avenues of further investigation for a production-ready Linux distribution that doesn't force the use of systemd? Or can anyone provide anecdotes of running Slackware or Gentoo in production, along with any problems that have cropped up?
